newsitem.title: UK: Ldn precious metals retreat under selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Ldn precious metals retreat under selling pressure.

text.p: Gold lost its grip above $349.00 on Tuesday afternoon, retreating back slightly as selling pressure began to weigh on the precious metals complex.
Bullion was indicated lower at $347.90/$348.40 in afternoon exchanges after weakness in silver having fixed unchanged from the morning at $349.10 an ounce.
Palladium, which spearheaded a rally this week after the prospect of new delays in Russian supplies to Japan, also came off the top but was still quoted $2.25 up at $153.50/$154.50.
"There's a lot of borrowing. People are squeezing it a bit because everyone is short, spot and forward," said a dealer.
Gold's descent to the middle of the trading range justified some dealers' views that upside prospects were capped given the dollar's gains against the yen and mark, and grim chart signals.
"I can't see gold going too much higher. Even if it does go through $350.00 there would be a lot of selling," said one.
But support was seen holding around $347.00/$347.50 after it survived a test of the downside below $347.00 last week.
"There is a bit of pressure on the market. Silver came off, everything came off," commented one London dealer.
Losses were mainly led by silver which dipped back below $4.80 chart resistance to $4.76/$4.78.
It was seen heading towards $4.72/$4.74 area, which coincides with Monday's close after an intraday high of $4.83.
Palladium remained the star attraction, and as it bubbled above $153.00 dealers saw scope for a move toward $160.00 in the rare metal, used mainly in autocatalysts and electronics.
Fuelling the rise is continued delay in Russia over renegotiating PGM sale contracts to Japan, the world's biggest buyer, after they expired at the beginning of the year.
"It scuppered any plans for getting palladium into Japan... even if they did start re-supplying there would be a lot of (backlog of) demand in Japan," said one London dealer.
In palladium, Swiss buyers were spearheading the demand and borrowing, although speculative interest was also cited.
Karen Jones, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston said bullion was due for a bounce to the top of its range at $350.00 after underlying support levels survived downside tests.
But she described the market as "neutral" for the moment.
Silver's prospects were similar, with a downside bias still intact although some gains toward $4.90 were possible.
"There may be a bit of room on the upside but over next week or so it may try lower again," said a London-based dealer.
